lesson.subject: general-knowledge
lesson.title: Trees and Forests
lesson.summary: Find out why trees matter, where the world's forests are and how to plant for the future.

standards.text: Describe and understand key aspects of physical geography, including vegetation belts and the water cycle; understand how humans affect the environment

success_criteria: I can name five benefits of trees
I can show where forests grow
I can plan how to plant a tree
lesson.real_life: Pakistan's Billion Tree Tsunami in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the deodar forests of Swat, British woodlands, and the encouragement to plant trees in Islam.

warm_up.prompt: Which gas do trees give out?
A pine tree is a conifer.

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: why are trees and forests important?
blocks.say: Today we ask why trees matter. They give us air, food, homes and shade.

blocks.alt: A single large leafy tree with a rounded crown standing in a bright green field under a deep blue sky
blocks.caption: A broadleaf tree in a field. It gives shade and homes for wildlife.
blocks.credit: Photo by kevin davis on Unsplash
blocks.say: This broadleaf tree stands alone in a field. It gives shade, and homes for birds and insects.

blocks.markdown: A **forest** is a large area covered with trees.
blocks.say: Trees take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen. We need oxygen to breathe.

scenes.caption: Clean air.
scenes.say: Trees give out oxygen. They also take in carbon dioxide from the air.

scenes.caption: Food.
scenes.say: Trees give us food, such as fruit, nuts and shade for crops.

scenes.caption: Homes.
scenes.say: Trees give homes to birds, insects and many other animals.

question.prompt: What do trees give out that we need to breathe?

blocks.markdown: **Carbon** is stored in trees, so forests help the climate.
blocks.say: Trees store carbon in their wood and leaves. This helps to slow climate change.
Tree roots hold soil in place. Leaves slow the rain, so floods and erosion are less likely.

scenes.caption: Carbon in.
scenes.say: A tree takes in carbon dioxide from the air as it grows.

scenes.caption: Stored.
scenes.say: The carbon is stored in the trunk, branches and roots.

scenes.caption: Soil.
scenes.say: Roots hold the soil, so hillsides do not wash away.

question.prompt: Trees can help to slow climate change by storing carbon.

blocks.title: Faiza plants a ber tree
blocks.transcript: Faiza has a ber sapling to plant in Islamabad. The ber is a native tree. It suits the local climate. She digs a hole, plants the sapling and waters it. Years later, the tree gives cool shade. Birds and insects make their homes in its branches. The tree takes in carbon and gives out oxygen. Neighbours enjoy the fruit. It is a lasting kindness. One tree helps. Many trees together help the whole planet.
blocks.caption: Faiza plants a ber tree in Islamabad and learns how a single tree gives shade, homes and cleaner air.

points: Trees give oxygen, food and homes
blocks.say: Let us remember. Trees give air, food, homes and shade. They also store carbon and protect the soil.

blocks.markdown: Forests are found where there is enough water and warmth.
blocks.say: Forests cover about one third of the world's land. They grow on every continent except Antarctica.

blocks.markdown: Tropical rainforests are hot and wet all year.
blocks.say: The biggest tropical rainforests are the Amazon, the Congo and those in South-East Asia.

scenes.caption: Tropical.
scenes.say: Tropical rainforests lie near the Equator. They are hot and wet.

scenes.caption: Temperate.
scenes.say: Temperate forests grow in places such as the UK and Europe.

scenes.caption: Northern.
scenes.say: Northern forests of pine and fir stretch across cold lands.

question.explanation: Tropical rainforests are near the Equator.

blocks.caption: Evergreen conifers and broadleaf trees in mist. Many mountain forests look like this.
blocks.credit: Photo by Filip Zrnzević on Unsplash
blocks.say: Pakistan has forests too. Deodar trees grow in the mountains, and shisham and ber grow on the plains.
Forests are changing. Cutting trees for farms, wood and roads makes forests smaller.

scenes.caption: Planting.
scenes.say: Billion Tree Tsunami planted more than a billion trees in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

scenes.caption: Loss.
scenes.say: Cutting forests for farming and roads removes habitats.

scenes.caption: Different.
scenes.say: Different places lose or gain forest at different speeds.

blocks.markdown: Leaves and bark are clues to a tree's name.
blocks.say: We can identify trees by their leaves, bark and shape. Look closely, like a detective.

scenes.caption: Oak.
scenes.say: An oak has lobed leaves and rough, deep-grooved bark.

scenes.caption: Pine.
scenes.say: A pine has long needles in bunches and scaly bark.

scenes.caption: Shape.
scenes.say: Look at the shape. Some trees are round, some are tall and narrow.

blocks.title: Tree clues
blocks.goal: Watch the order, then copy it. It gets longer each time!
blocks.say: Broadleaf trees have wide, flat leaves. Conifers have needles and cones. Warm up your memory.

blocks.markdown: **Evergreen** trees keep their leaves; **deciduous** trees shed them.
blocks.say: Some trees are evergreen and keep leaves all year. Deciduous trees lose their leaves in autumn.

scenes.caption: Broadleaf.
scenes.say: Broadleaf trees include oak and shisham. Most shed leaves, but holly keeps them.

scenes.caption: Conifer.
scenes.say: Conifers such as pine and deodar keep needles all year.

scenes.caption: Exceptions.
scenes.say: A few conifers, such as larch, lose their needles in winter.

blocks.text: Stop 1: Choose a site and a native tree

blocks.markdown: A **native** tree belongs naturally to the area.
blocks.say: A native tree grows naturally in a place. Native trees suit local weather and help local wildlife.

blocks.markdown: Planting a tree is a kind act for the future.
blocks.say: In Pakistan, Muslims are encouraged to plant trees. Fruit and shade from a tree can be a lasting charity.

scenes.caption: A site.
scenes.say: Choose a safe site, such as a school field or a park, with space to grow.

scenes.caption: Native tree.
scenes.say: Choose a native tree, such as shisham, ber or neem, that suits your area.

scenes.caption: Prepare.
scenes.say: Ask permission first. Then prepare a hole and good soil.

options.text: It suits the local climate and wildlife

blocks.alt: A young green seedling with serrated leaves growing in dark soil
blocks.caption: A young seedling in soil. A sapling needs care to grow into a tree.
blocks.credit: Photo by Rainier Ridao on Unsplash
blocks.say: A sapling needs water, protection and time. Measure its height every month to track growth.

scenes.caption: Water.
scenes.say: Water the sapling regularly, especially in the dry season.

scenes.caption: Protect.
scenes.say: Protect it with a guard from animals and strong sun.

scenes.caption: Measure.
scenes.say: Measure it every month and write it down. Share the job with neighbours.
